before.supportingExcerpt: Functional tumour volume (FTV) in research is a calculated volume of voxels inside a selected region that meet specified enhancement and processing rules. Changing thresholds, postcontrast time, region, software or registration can change which voxels qualify. Li and colleagues studied enhancement thresholds and recurrence-free survival in a particular breast cohort. DCE names an acquisition, BPE describes background, NME describes morphology, and FTV names a calculation. They are not four estimates of one quantity, and the word functional does not turn the calculated volume into an amount of viable tumour.
before.explanation: The exact cited paragraphs carry this source-first obligation at the named population, measurement, fictional-example or guideline-version scope. Their quoted anchors and the recorded source limits are part of the assessment; mere link presence is not the proof. Source scope: Complete Li abstract and targeted methods paragraphs. Distinguishes the method, inputs and units; no universal threshold or viability conversion.
